description:
I am an individual participant interested in space exploration, technology and storytelling. My goal is to create an engaging and visually appealing project showcasing NASA equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars, exploring its history, purpose and scientific achievements.

I have an IT background and an interest in software development, web technologies and visual presentation.
summary:
Lunar Echoes explores the legacy of human and robotic space exploration by highlighting equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. From lunar modules and scientific instruments to robotic landers and rovers, the project reveals the stories behind machines that helped expand our understanding of the Solar System.

It focuses on the purpose of these technologies, the missions they supported, the scientific discoveries they enabled and their historical significance. By bringing attention to these often-overlooked objects, Lunar Echoes aims to preserve the legacy of space exploration and make its achievements more accessible to a wider audience, especially younger generations interested in science and technology.
details:
Lunar Echoes focuses on documenting and exploring the legacy of space exploration equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars.

The project highlights selected objects from historical NASA missions, including lunar landers, scientific instruments, robotic rovers and other mission hardware. It examines their original purposes, operational roles, scientific contributions and historical importance.

Special attention is given to the Apollo missions and robotic Mars exploration, showing how equipment left on other celestial bodies continues to represent important milestones in human technological development.

The project combines historical research, NASA documentation and visual materials to communicate scientific knowledge in an accessible and engaging way.

Its main objective is to raise awareness of the often-overlooked legacy of space exploration and demonstrate how past missions continue to contribute to our understanding of the Solar System.
